standard_prerequisites.name: Simplicial sets and homotopy of morphisms
standard_prerequisites.statement: The category of simplicial sets, the standard simplices and their boundaries, and homotopy defined through Delta[1] times X.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the setting of the statement and of the displayed square (source lines 5860-5861, 5866-5872).

standard_prerequisites.name: The lifting property of a trivial Kan fibration
standard_prerequisites.statement: A trivial Kan fibration lifts every solid diagram whose horizontal map is termwise injective, and in particular admits a right inverse and a homotopy from the composite to the identity (the author's lemma-trivial-kan, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the right inverse g and fills the dotted arrow of the proof (source lines 5865, 5878-5879).

standard_prerequisites.name: The boundary of the 1-simplex
standard_prerequisites.statement: For every n the set of n-simplices of the boundary of Delta[1] times X is the coproduct X_n coproduct X_n, corresponding to the two endpoints.
standard_prerequisites.use: It lets the top horizontal arrow be specified by id_X on one copy and g f on the other (source lines 5873-5875).

core_obligations: Choose a right inverse: use the lifting property to produce g : Y to X with f g = id (source lines 5865-5866).

Build the square: define the top horizontal arrow on the two boundary copies as id_X and g f and the bottom arrow through f and the projection Delta[1] to Delta[0], and verify commutativity using f g f = f (source lines 5866-5877).
Fill and conclude: apply the lifting property once more to get the dotted arrow, which is the homotopy from g f to the identity (source lines 5878-5879).

proof_roadmap.step: Choose a right inverse g of f by the lifting property.
Write down the square with (id_X, g f) on the boundary and check it commutes.
Fill the dotted arrow and read off the homotopy.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-trivial-kan-homotopy at source lines 5858-5862: every trivial Kan fibration f : X to Y of simplicial sets is a homotopy equivalence. The proof at source lines 5864-5880 uses the lifting property of the previous lemma to choose a right inverse g : Y to X, builds the square whose top horizontal map is (id_X, g f) on the boundary of the 1-simplex times X and whose bottom map is the composite through f and the projection Delta[1] to Delta[0], observes that the square commutes because f g f = f, and fills the dotted arrow by the lifting property again, which is precisely the required homotopy from g f to the identity. It is short; the substance is the correct bookkeeping of the two boundary copies of X and the use of the lifting property twice.
